newsitem.title: UK: Key points from 1996 UK budget.
newsitem.headline: Key points from 1996 UK budget.

text.p: The following is a summary of key points from the last British budget, unveiled by Conservative Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke on November 26, 1996.
-- Basic rate of income tax was cut to 23 percent from 24 percent. Personal allowance was raised by 280 stg to 4,045 stg.
-- Corporation Tax on small company profits was reduced to 23 percent from 24 percent.
-- Capital gains tax exempt amount was increased to 6,500 stg from 6,300
-- Threshold for inheritance tax was raised to 215,000 stg from 200,000.
-- Tax relief on profit-related pay to be reduced from 1998 and abolished by 2000.
-- National insurance contributions by employers were reduced to 10 percent from 10.2 as announced in the 1995 budget.
-- Petrol and diesel duties were increased by three pence a litre.
-- Duty on beer and wine was frozen, tax on spirits was cut by four percent.
-- Tax on cigarettes was increased by 15 pence per packet.
-- Insurance premium tax was raised to four percent from 2.5 percent.
-- Public sector borrowing requirement (PSBR) was forecast at 26.4 billion stg in 1996/97 and 19.2 billion in 1997/98.
-- General government expenditure was estimated at 308.5 billion stg in 1996/97 and 319 billion in 1997/98.
-- General government receipts were estimated at 280.9 billion stg in 1996/97 and 299.4 billion in 1997/98.
-- Clarke said the budget cut public spending by two billion stg in 1997/98 and would generate an extra 500 million stg in revenue.
-- GDP growth was forecast at 2.5 percent in 1996 and 3.5 percent in 1997.
